population.definition: Population of the Cairo Governorate (Muhafazah al-Qahirah) recorded in the 2017 general census of population, housing and establishments (census date 28 March 2017) conducted by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) of Egypt, tabulated via citypopulation.de. The urban agglomeration of Greater Cairo (spanning Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia governorates) counted 20,165,732 residents at the same census, making it the most populous urban agglomeration on the African continent.

source.title: Egypt: Governorates, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2017)
source.publisher: CityPopulation (credits Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics, Egypt)

facts.claim: Cairo was founded in 969 AD by the Fatimid military commander Jawhar al-Siqilli under Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, naming it al-Qahirah ('The Victorious') as the new imperial capital.

source.title: Historic Cairo
source.quote: founded in the 10th century by the Fatimids

facts.claim: Construction of Al-Azhar Mosque began in 970 AD, soon developing into a renowned center of higher Islamic learning and one of the oldest continuously operating universities in the world.

source.title: Jami' al-Azhar (Al-Azhar Mosque)
source.quote: begun in 970 by Jawhar al-Siqilli, the Fatimid conqueror of Egypt

facts.claim: In 1176 Sultan Salah al-Din (Saladin) began construction of the Citadel of Cairo on the Mokattam hills to fortify the city against Crusader armies and establish a centralized seat of government.

source.title: The Citadel of Saladin
source.publisher: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Arab Republic of Egypt
source.quote: begun in 1176 by Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi

facts.claim: In 1382 Emir Djaharks al-Khalili built a grand caravanserai on the former site of the Fatimid royal cemetery, which expanded over subsequent centuries into the historic market quarter of Khan el-Khalili.

source.title: Khan al-Khalili
source.quote: established around 1382 by Emir Djaharks al-Khalili

facts.claim: In 1902 the purpose-built neoclassical Museum of Egyptian Antiquities was inaugurated on Tahrir Square, designed by French architect Marcel Dourgnon to house Egypt's pharaonic treasures.

source.title: The Egyptian Museum in Tahrir
source.publisher: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Arab Republic of Egypt
source.quote: inaugurated in 1902, designed by French architect Marcel Dourgnon

places.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
places.what: The historic Fatimid congregational mosque founded in 970 CE in the heart of Historic Cairo. Over the centuries it grew into the most influential university and authority for Sunni Islamic scholarship globally.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: One of the oldest continually operating universities in the world

source.title: Jami' al-Azhar (Al-Azhar Mosque)
source.quote: one of the oldest operating institutions of higher learning

places.name: Citadel of Saladin
places.what: A massive medieval stone fortress perched on the Mokattam hills, founded in 1176 by Salah al-Din. For nearly 700 years it served as the royal seat of Egyptian government, and features the 19th-century alabaster Mosque of Muhammad Ali.

source.title: The Citadel of Saladin
source.publisher: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Egypt

places.name: Khan el-Khalili
places.what: A renowned historic market and bazaar district in Islamic Cairo, originating from a 1382 Mamluk caravanserai built by Emir Djaharks al-Khalili. It is celebrated for traditional metalwork, spices, stained glass, textiles and historical coffeehouses like El Fishawy (operating since 1773).

places.name: Egyptian Museum in Tahrir
places.what: The historic Museum of Egyptian Antiquities on Tahrir Square, inaugurated in November 1902 in a purpose-built neoclassical palace designed by French architect Marcel Dourgnon. It houses more than 120,000 pharaonic antiquities, papyri and royal statues.
